he expel the third, we shall leave that house for another, which we will treat the same way we treated
the first house. We shall make the round, going from one house to the next, in other words the whole city,
until the people conclude that the great harm which is affecting them
arises from the cats. If they conclude this, they will not restrict themselves to killing only the cats
that are in the houses. The King and the rest of rats did what
the vizier had advised. Before six months passed, all the cats that were in the city
and its vicinities had perished. That generation of people went by and after them another group grew up hating
cats: every time they discovered some corruption caused by mice, they said,
‘Look Could a cat have gone through the city?’ Also, whenever it happened
that people or animals got inflicted by a disease, they said, ‘It almost seems as if some cat passed through the city.’
In this way that the rats rid themselves of the horror of the cats and were at peace from them <> If this weak and lowly animal could conceive of such trickery, so as to
get rid of his enemy and removing harm from himself, then hope must not be lost
in man, who is the smartest, most perfect, and wisest living being, can obtain from his enemy
what he wants using his ingenuity and good planning.
The Chapter of the Cat and Rat

p.n: The King Asks about Escaping Enemies
